summary:
H3 measured against the whole catalogue at v33-frozen (0065f1e2). The catalogue has 329 entries, not 330: the 330th '### ' heading is 'The 50 rated medium or low'. Of the 329, 38 are in scope (13 yes, 25 part), 5 are about the language pack only, and 286 are outside the three sections. The 38 entries are 30 distinct defects when grouped by the catalogue's own 'Repeats' notes.

Every in-scope entry got a check that a machine runs. The checks are in P/h3/issuecheck33.js. Each one is true on OLD for at least one language, and all 28 checks were run on OLD and NEW for all 20 languages. Five new variations (no-cache, one-wrap, only-wrap, feat-text, ref-dollar) were added so that S22, U52, U53, V27, U102 and M37 could show at all. D04 shows in no variation and was only read.

Results for the 13 ported languages, counted per entry:
- 29 are fixed by shared code only ('once'). This includes N04/U06/M04 and M14 under the rule's exemption for type and constructor printers.
- 1 needed lines of each language's own (S13): the testMock fact in 13 Syntax files, citations in 20 forms files, and a fix to the ts/js runtime Config fragments.
- 6 are NOT fixed: X3, S22, U52, U53, V27 and U102. All six are in ReadmeRefFeatures.ts or FeatureDocs.ts, which were already shared at main and which the prototype never touched. NEW still shows each of them in all 20 languages. Each needs one shared edit.
- 2 show only in an unported language: N11/M35, the ts fence on js pages.

The H3 ratio, counted per entry over 36 entries (fixed or should be):
- Per-language edit, by the brief's rule: 1/36 = 2.8%. Strictest reading, which also counts the type printers and go's printer: 5/36 = 13.9%.
- With the six unfixed entries counted against the proposal: 7/36 = 19.4% by the rule, 11/36 = 30.6% strictest.

Counted per distinct defect (29): 3.4%, 10.3%, 24.1% and 31.0%, in the same order.

Verdict: H3 is not refuted on its per-language criterion. It is not confirmed as stated, because 6 of 36 in-scope entries are not fixed at all at the frozen state. It is not decided until the six shared edits are made and the seven remaining ports pass issuecheck33.js.
verdict: H3 is not decided. It is not refuted on its criterion: of the 36 in-scope entries that are fixed or should be, 1 (S13) needed a per-language edit. That is 2.8% by the brief's rule (3.4% per distinct defect), or 13.9% under the strictest reading that also counts the 13 type printers and go's printer. But H3 claims more than that: 'the catalogued issues in those sections are fixed once, for every language'. Six in-scope entries (X3 S22 U52 U53 V27 U102, 17% of entries, 21% of distinct defects) are not fixed at all at v33-frozen; NEW still shows them in all 20 languages. Counted against the proposal, that gives 19.4% by the rule, past the 10% line. My reading: the per-language criterion holds (about 3%), because the six unfixed entries each need one shared edit in a component that was already shared at main, not an edit per language. But the frozen state does not show 'fixed once', and the prototype never took the features half of the REFERENCE into scope. What would decide it: make the six shared edits; port the last seven languages; run `node P/h3/issuecheck33.js P/h3/out --ported <all 20>` after regenerating out/new and require exit 0, js clearing N11/M35 included; and count S13's testMock lines in the seven ports (expected: one Syntax line each).

my_reading:
The right reading for H3's criterion ('still need a per-language edit') counts the six unfixed entries as shared edits, not per-language edits. Each sits in ReadmeRefFeatures.ts or FeatureDocs.ts, which have been one shared file for all 20 languages since main, and each needs one shared change. The type printer and go's printer are exempt under the brief's own rule: a provider has to print types and constructors anyway, and under the design it never sees target.name, so it cannot repeat N04's defect. By that reading the per-language share is 2.8% per entry (3.4% per distinct defect), well under 10%, and the criterion holds.

H3 as worded, however, says the issues ARE fixed once. At the frozen state 6 of 36 are not fixed at all; NEW still prints each of them in all 20 languages. I therefore call H3 not decided rather than confirmed.

The one per-language entry, S13, needs a declared runtime fact in every provider: zig and clojure ship the mock whatever the model, the rest do not. It also needed a ts/js runtime change. That is the design working as intended (a runtime difference is data), but it costs 20 lines plus 20 citations.
other_direction:
Defects the prototype found that the catalogue does not list (read from the records, not re-run):

1. **Sentence review** (s3b-sentences.txt, brief6). 14 false ids, which are 6 distinct false sentences: the env-var sentence, direct's err, explain:true, two test-client sentences, and action returns. All 6 were fixed in shared code (sfix 2608dd45). Two also needed per-language declarations: testMock in every provider, and a truth read for direct's ok in c, go, rust and zig, later swift and ocaml. One needed a runtime fix in ts/js (b09502f1). So 4 of 6 were fixed by one shared edit alone, and 2 by a shared edit plus per-language facts. The review also found 8 per-language defects of single providers (c getp, elixir list heading, clojure lazy seq, zig switch, c undeclared vars, rust code span, a rust note and a zig note). These are by nature per-language, except the 'Instance Functions' heading, which became one shared rule (decision 10).
2. **Wave 1** (s3b-wave1-consolidated.md). The 14 numbered shared decisions of brief7 were each made once in shared code. Most were additive optional facts that the languages having the property declare: accessor.cached for lua; streamSignal; copy on the match getter; the field flag and bare member name for ocaml; the deleted mark; swift's unwrap; the utility copy, where ts declares copy:false. The freeze report says the per-language parts were 'all facts, not prose'.
3. **s2-ref uncatalogued** (5 items):
   - backtick leak, Actions shown in ts only, direct ctrl: fixed by one shared edit each.
   - stream missing: per-language; every provider declares the member, enforced by the guard.
   - perl ->{id}: shared showFields (decision 3) plus the perl port.

   Totals for these three sources: 25 items; about 17 fixed by one shared edit; about 8 needed per-language lines or are per-language by nature.

Regressions and residues on NEW, found while reading:
- The REFERENCE ordering note still prints escaped backticks ('\\`cost\\` activated before \\`cache\\`') in all 20 languages, on OLD and NEW. The s2 'backtick' fix covered only '\\`feature\\`'.
- log's REFERENCE section still says 'Set `feature.log.active` to true' although log is on by default. This is uncatalogued and on OLD too.
- The freeze report's own open items: 4 changed sentences have no verdict (42aedb7ce3, fe4d5d27e7, fdfa305bc4, 0612fc4d79); 1 unreviewed lua sentence; attacks still accepted (a zig .ok/.err swap, py list(), rb Hash, a wrong step number or article). These are matching holes, not page defects shown on NEW.
- Earlier regressions I re-checked on NEW are gone: c's REFERENCE load example now checks NULL; swift's list(nil, nil) is restored; zig field types match OLD (1 `any` each, on doc-crud).

No new regression of a catalogued kind was found by issuecheck33: no check is clean on OLD and true on NEW for any language.
